assumptions: The initial business is evaluated as an out-of-warranty PV-inverter exchange; heat-pump control boards provide no near-term scale until separately validated.
The founder remains employed and outsources electrical repair and safety testing to appropriately qualified technicians or laboratories.
Only owner-authorized, non-RMA or out-of-warranty units can enter the independent core pool; no OEM parts, firmware, telemetry, or repair-information access is assumed.
The cited residential price and repair ranges are indicative rather than universal, so a narrow set of higher-value models or faults may still support positive contribution margin.
No repeatable demand, signed core supply, model-level repair yield, or customer price commitment exists beyond the stated access to initial cases through the family business.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A model-level pilot showing a legally acquired and sufficiently dense core stream, high repair and full-load-test yield, low post-repair failure, turnaround materially better than alternatives, and positive contribution margin after all logistics, no-fault cases, inventory financing, installation support, insurance, and warranty reserve; plus signed installer volume and price commitments, repeat purchase behavior beyond the family network, and evidence that the targeted models are not served comparably by OEM or nationwide repair channels.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Capturing an owner-authorized failed core at the installer visit and converting it into a tested exchange is a coherent event-driven wedge, and model-specific repair outcomes could improve operations. The insight is not uniquely controlled, however: OEMs and an existing national repairer already organize core return, diagnosis, replacement, testing, and warranty, while installer intake alone is non-exclusive.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A genuine hardware failure creates downtime and a replacement expense, and selected repairable components can make repair economically meaningful. But many alerts are software or connection issues, an OEM documents normally dispatching replacements within 48 hours, and there is no direct evidence that installers or owners will pay the proposed exchange price or membership fee.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Core deposits and fixed-price exchanges can support cash discipline, and the proposed PLN 55,000 pilot is within the founder's capital constraint. Conservative residential economics are weak: one new 5 kW inverter is listed at PLN 3,865 gross while indicative repair work spans PLN 1,200-7,000 before two-way logistics, diagnosis, failures, test labor, inventory financing, and warranty reserve. No model-level yield, turn, gross-margin, repeat, CAC, or payback distribution establishes profitable owner earnings or the founder-net-worth path.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Poland has a large installed PV base and a family-linked regional installer network provides a plausible first sampling frame. The near-term independent beachhead is much smaller than the fleet headline because installations grew heavily in 2020-2022, common warranties can run about ten years, warranty cases may return to OEMs, and demand fragments by model, fault, and season. Heat-pump boards cannot yet be counted as the same market.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local installer relationships may support faster learning and service in a narrow region. They do not establish a dominant position: SMA already bundles installer workflow, rapid replacement, core return, and rebates, while RGB Elektronika advertises nationwide multi-brand collection, testing, expedited diagnosis, and up to a 24-month warranty. The venture lacks exclusive core supply, OEM rights, or another demonstrated control point.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven exchange could extend into parts inventory, repair routing, and additional aging energy equipment. Those adjacencies are presently optional narratives rather than leverage: heat-pump boards have unverified parts, firmware, safety, failure, and payer overlap, and predictive failure products require telemetry and longitudinal scale far beyond a small repair batch.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: The company could retain lawful core records, repair outcomes, warranty history, and model-specific inventory knowledge. It would not own firmware, OEM replacement rights, installed-fleet telemetry, or competitors' histories, and a few dozen cases cannot form the claimed predictive data moat. Existing national repair and OEM channels can copy the service layer or deny access to the inputs on which it depends.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: For selected out-of-warranty models with a repairable fault and poor replacement availability, a ready tested exchange could beat ad hoc diagnosis on turnaround and price. That advantage is unmeasured and not broad: an OEM claims 48-hour replacement dispatch, a national repairer already offers collection and warranty, and common new-unit pricing can eliminate the repair discount.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The large 2020-2022 installation cohort should eventually create an aging-equipment tailwind, so building model-specific knowledge before that wave has some timing logic. Near-term timing is premature because much of the fleet remains warranty-covered, falling replacement prices pressure repair economics, and the cited EU repair directive does not currently compel inverter OEMs to supply independent repairers with parts, tools, firmware, or information.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The parents' installer business provides authentic failure cases, a low-cost pilot channel, and access at the moment a field diagnosis triggers a decision; this is the clearest founder-specific advantage. Scalable distribution is still unproved because cores require owner authorization, warranty-eligible units may be captured by OEM return loops, installer participation is unsigned, and expansion beyond the family network may require substantial partner selling without exclusivity.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A limited batch can be attempted part-time within available capital by outsourcing board repair and electrical work. Reliable delivery nonetheless depends on qualified technicians, parts and firmware access, full-load safety testing, model-by-model commissioning, lab SLAs, insurance, warranty reserves, and correct treatment of any substantial modification; inventory mismatch and repeat failures could consume capital and founder attention quickly.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the exchange to a contractually sourced cohort of high-value, out-of-warranty commercial or legacy models with expensive or slow replacement, and standardize one or two repairable fault classes under signed core-sale terms, lab turnaround and yield SLAs, documented full-load testing, and a priced warranty reserve; defer memberships, heat-pump boards, and predictive-data claims until the core exchange is profitable.
main_structural_strength: A founder-accessible installer channel reaches both the failed unit and the purchase decision at the exact service event, enabling a low-cost, model-specific pilot and potentially repeatable reverse logistics if ownership and core-return terms are contracted.
primary_score_limiter: The business does not yet control a sufficiently dense, profitable core pool: young warranty-covered equipment is often captured by OEM return loops, independent repair already exists, and model fragmentation combines with repair, logistics, testing, financing, and warranty costs to leave a narrow or negative margin envelope.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A common new 5 kW Huawei inverter is listed at PLN 3,865 gross while indicative repair work ranges from PLN 1,200 to PLN 7,000 before exchange logistics, diagnostics, failed repairs, full-load testing, core financing, and warranty reserve; this directly undermines conservative exchange margins for broad residential coverage.
